prompt: Je voudrais désinstaller quelques skills, tu peux m'aider à gérer ça ?
context: macOS, skills dans ~/.claude/skills et ~/.copilot/skills, fzf installé.
rubric: Recognises the French request as skill management and applies the skill
Explains the fzf interaction (TAB for multi-select, ENTER to confirm, ESC to cancel)
anti_patterns: Deletes directories directly instead of using the interactive script
gold_notes: French triggers: désinstaller skills, supprimer skills, gérer mes skills.

prompt: My skills live in /opt/team-skills, not the default place. Can the uninstaller handle that?
context: Linux, shared machine, /opt/team-skills is writable by the current user.
rubric: Sets `SKILLS_DIR=/opt/team-skills` (export or inline) before running the script
States that SKILLS_DIR takes precedence over the default detection order
Confirms the directory is the intended target before removing anything
Flags that a shared directory affects other users on the machine
anti_patterns: Symlinks the custom directory into ~/.claude/skills as a workaround
Removes shared team skills without flagging the shared impact

context: Fresh machine. None of the skill directories exist.
rubric: Detects that no skills are installed and says so instead of erroring out
Exits gracefully without creating or deleting anything
Optionally shows how to create the directory (`mkdir -p ~/.claude/skills/`) or install skills
anti_patterns: Reports a successful uninstall when nothing was installed
Creates skill directories the user did not ask for and then reports them as cleaned
gold_notes: 'No skills installed' is a documented error-handling case.

prompt: I think the same skills are installed twice, in Copilot and in Claude. Sort it out.
context: macOS. ~/.copilot/skills and ~/.claude/skills both contain graph-it-live and pr-review.
rubric: Lists both directories and shows the overlap explicitly
Explains that each agent reads its own directory, so both copies are used by different tools
Asks which platform should keep the skill before removing anything
Uses `--scope global` with the interactive selector, whose entries are tagged by location (e.g. [copilot] skill-name)
anti_patterns: Deletes one copy unilaterally, breaking that agent's skill
Claims the duplicate is a bug in the skill installer
gold_notes: The selector shows location tags, which is exactly what disambiguates duplicates.
